previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a complex medical history including acute myeloid leukemia in remission after stem cell transplant, anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy with severely reduced ejection fraction (10–13%), end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection, and cryptogenic organizing pneumonia on supplemental oxygen, was admitted for recurrent syncope. The episodes, occurring daily and recently at rest, were evaluated with telemetry, echocardiogram, EEG, and CT angiography. No arrhythmias, seizures, or pulmonary embolism were found. The syncope was determined to be multifactorial, primarily due to orthostatic hypotension from end-stage heart failure, with possible vagal and psychogenic components. His adrenal insufficiency was confirmed with a suboptimal cortisol response, leading to an increase in prednisone from 2 mg to 5 mg daily. He remained stable without further syncopal events, continued his vancomycin taper for C. diff, and was cleared for swallowing. Goals of care were discussed, and code status was updated to DNR with intubation allowed. He was discharged home with services, on a stable medication regimen, with follow-up in cardiology, endocrinology, and primary care.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ is a ___ year old man with a complex medical 
history notable for AML in remission, ESRD on HD (MWF, missed on 
___, HFrEF (10%) ___ anthrocycline treatment toxicity, 
recurrent C.diff on prophylactic vancomycin, and COP (home O2 
4L) who was discharged on ___ for an admission for syncope, 
re-admitted with syncope and worsened shortness of breath, 
transferred to CCU for hypotension during dialysis and need for 
CRRT, with hospital course complicated by hypoxic respiratory 
failure requiring bilateral chest tube placement

Patient with severe anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy with a 
left ventricular ejection fraction of 10%, multiple 
hospitalizations for heart failure and cardiogenic shock in 
past. Patient had not been on cardiac medications as an 
outpatient due to inability to tolerate. He has not shown 
improvement with dobutamine in the past. He was not an LVAD 
candidate as per the Heart Failure team. His current 
exacerbation was likely in the setting of inadequate volume 
removal with HD, however he was unable to tolerate it due to 
hypotension. Patient was placed on CRRT which he did not 
tolerate well. Per renal recommendations, it would be unlikely 
that he would be able to tolerate HD given that his pressor 
requirement was unable to be weaned. After multiple discussions 
with his family, decision was made to transition patient to CMO 
and patient expired subsequently with family at the bedside.
